name: Diamond Mountain
summary: Two fire towers on Diamond Mountain near Sloatsburg: a 1935 steel tower and a 1966 Aermotor replacement, removed 1986; no source describes the summit site today.
design: Steel tower built in 1935 from the steel of the old Bear Mountain tower; 1966 replacement was an 80-foot Aermotor LS 40 with louvered aluminum windows in the cab
status_note: Both towers removed: the first taken down in 1955, the second removed in 1986.

access.note: A 2020 hiking account describes trails in Harriman State Park that reach the summit. The account does not describe the tower site itself.

visit.trail_note: A yellow-blazed Diamond Mountain Tower Trail and the HTS Trail reach the summit. No source describes any remaining tower structure.

events.note: Palisades State Park Commission built a steel tower from the steel of the old Bear Mountain tower
First tower taken down; its steel stored for safe keeping
Park Commission erected an 80-foot Aermotor LS 40 tower
Second tower removed after standing twenty years
DEC deactivated most fire observation stations; the detection system that included Diamond Mountain came to a halt
Steel from the Diamond Mountain towers reused at Sterling Fire Tower when Sterling Forest State Park was created
